scope: Bounded source cross-check of the adopted rules in engineering/design/ux-grammar.md against selected first-party design guidance and the existing CourtWork contracts. Eight pages were opened directly; this is not a new design-system survey.

sources.title: Content Fundamentals
sources.source_type: First-party design-system content guidance in an archived repository
sources.revision_or_date: Repository archived 2026-09-11; source file retained at the archive's main branch
sources.quality: Primary first-party guidance for Shopify's design system; use as a documented practice example because the repository is archived.
sources.scope_checked: Content Fundamentals, especially the copy-purpose and editing guidance around lines 211-249.
observed: Recommends considering the purpose and value of each word, using supporting copy only when needed, and editing away text whose meaning is already carried by the interface.
sources.application_inference: Supports a deliberate deletion pass and text-with-a-purpose rule in UX-01; it does not establish CourtWork's permitted text roles as a universal taxonomy.
limits: The repository is archived and should not be presented as a currently maintained standard.
Its content guidance does not decide CourtWork domain names, permission disclosure, error recovery, or acceptance semantics.

sources.title: Writing for user interfaces
sources.quality: Primary published guidance for UK government services; older page, used only for the stated writing principles.
sources.scope_checked: Guidance on using short, clear interface text and reviewing products that require substantial instructional copy, especially around lines 81-122.
observed: Recommends starting with minimal UI text and improving the design where people need long instructions to use it.
sources.application_inference: Supports trying removal and redesign before adding explanatory copy; it does not justify hiding facts users need for decisions or recovery.
limits: The source is not a CourtWork interface contract and its advice is not a complete accessibility or disclosure specification.

sources.title: Contextual help
sources.quality: Primary pattern documentation maintained by GitLab; evidence of that system's pattern, not an industry-wide requirement.
sources.scope_checked: Placement and format guidance around lines 9-19 and 69-88.
observed: Distinguishes information that belongs directly in a task from optional details that can be available in a drawer, panel, or longer-lived documentation.
sources.application_inference: Supports UX-02's task-led progressive disclosure and the existing CourtWork default/context/technical layers.
limits: GitLab's specific component choices do not determine CourtWork's surface taxonomy, disclosure persistence, or authorization rules.

sources.title: Common actions
sources.source_type: First-party design-system pattern guidance on the preview domain
sources.quality: Primary Carbon guidance; treat as a vendor pattern and preview-domain publication, not CourtWork authority.
sources.scope_checked: Action semantics and selection around lines 26-76 and 98-128; deletion and feedback guidance around lines 165-185.
observed: Encourages action-specific labels and review of scope, persistence, permission, expected time, failure, and single-versus-bulk effects.
Uses Copy for creating an identical object instance, which differs from CourtWork's Copy-to-clipboard and Duplicate-to-create-a-copy mapping.
Discusses Apply as the last saved checkpoint in Reset guidance; it does not define Apply as universally transient or non-persistent.
Scales deletion confirmation to consequence and recovery, and gives a page-specific example recommending success feedback after a deletion.
sources.application_inference: Supports maintaining an explicit local action vocabulary and consequence-aware feedback/recovery checks. The differences in Copy, Apply, and success feedback show why CourtWork must keep its own owner contracts and retain contextual qualifiers such as 'usually'.
limits: Carbon action meanings are not universal semantics and must not overwrite CourtWork typed actions or wording.
Advice to use Undo assumes a real recovery path; it does not provide one for CourtWork.

sources.title: Switch Pattern
sources.publisher: World Wide Web Consortium (W3C) Web Accessibility Initiative
sources.revision_or_date: APG page accessed 2026-09-14; no revision date relied on
sources.quality: Primary W3C accessibility implementation guidance for the switch pattern; not a product permission model.
sources.scope_checked: Switch role, accessible name, checked state, and keyboard interaction around lines 21-50.
observed: Defines a switch as a binary on/off control with an accessible name, state exposure, and expected keyboard interaction.
sources.application_inference: Supports UX-03's semantic and accessibility requirements for a real writable binary value; it does not imply that a switch grants authorization or that read-only facts should look writable.
limits: The APG specifies interaction/accessibility behavior, not the business meaning or authority of the underlying state.

sources.title: Loading
sources.revision_or_date: Page date not relied on; accessed 2026-09-14
sources.quality: Primary loading-pattern guidance from GitHub; pattern donor, not evidence of CourtWork runtime capability.
sources.scope_checked: Loading strategy by duration, long-running work, and background work around lines 202-269 and 332-360.
observed: Uses approximate duration ranges to guide loading feedback and recommends keeping other interaction available for work lasting over ten seconds by moving it to a background process if possible.
sources.application_inference: Supports the distinction between a long wait and a nonblocking/background interaction only when that capability exists. The time threshold does not itself create a CourtWork Run state, worker, or background execution permission.
limits: Timing thresholds are pattern guidance, not service state definitions or a requirement to implement background processing.
The page does not establish CourtWork's cancellation, status, or ownership model.

sources.title: UX design for agents
sources.source_type: First-party product-design article about agent experiences
sources.revision_or_date: Article date not relied on; accessed 2026-09-14
sources.quality: First-party design guidance, not a normative accessibility or runtime specification.
sources.scope_checked: Agent activity and background work transparency/control around lines 92-102 and 123-135.
observed: Calls for agent activity and background actions to remain visible, inspectable, and controllable, with access to relevant status and context.
sources.application_inference: Supports UX-05/08's distinction between execution state, background placement, and inspectable provenance; it does not authorize a new CourtWork execution lane or history source.
limits: A product-design article does not define the owner service, typed actions, or formal review semantics for CourtWork.

sources.title: Carbon for AI
sources.source_type: First-party design-system guidance on the preview domain
sources.revision_or_date: Page date not relied on; accessed 2026-09-14
sources.quality: Primary Carbon guidance for its AI visual and interaction conventions; not a universal AI styling standard.
sources.scope_checked: AI transparency and styling around lines 50-64 and 95-107.
observed: Uses labels/explanations to communicate AI involvement and places explanations in the workflow when relevant or requested; its AI styling is tied to identifying AI use.
sources.application_inference: Supports UX-08's provenance and separation of AI-produced material from ordinary controls. Carbon's colors and visual treatment remain Carbon's dialect and do not establish CourtWork design tokens.
limits: Does not define CourtWork's model-run, source, tool, human-review, or formal-acceptance contracts.
The page is on Carbon's preview domain.

excluded_checks.title: Apple Human Interface Guidelines: Writing
excluded_checks.reason: The page returned a JavaScript-required shell in this check, so its writing guidance was not validated and is not used as evidence.

excluded_checks.title: Shopify Polaris Common Actions URL supplied in the conversation
excluded_checks.reason: It redirected to a general Shopify API index rather than a Common Actions guide; no claimed action mapping from that page is used.

research_limits: The saved conversation's search-result totals and unattributed quotations were not reproduced or used.

External design-system guidance supports or qualifies design choices; CourtWork contracts and Astra's recorded decision remain the authority for object, state, permission, persistence, recovery, and formal acceptance semantics.
This report does not claim full UX/accessibility acceptance or runtime verification.
